full_zh: 背景：我们的集成测试对一个共享的 Snowflake schema 跑迁移，所以两个工程师，或者两个 AI 编码 agent 会话，在不同分支上就会撞 DDL。没有 ticket，也没有 owner，是我自己决定去解决这个摩擦。
V1：我先从共享的 PUBLIC schema 克隆槽位。后来发现 PUBLIC 的状态取决于谁最后跑了迁移，槽位不可复现，所以必须重写。
V2：我写了 3 篇 ADR，建一个独立的 MAIN schema，同步到生产实际部署的 commit。我查 GitHub Deployments API 而不是 release tag，因为 tag 可能打了却没部署。每个槽位是 MAIN 的零拷贝克隆，约 2 秒，因为拷的是微分区元数据，不是数据。会话借一个槽位，跑迁移和测试，用完丢弃。
边界：跨库 stream 会受克隆顺序影响，所以先克隆 replication DB 再克隆 app DB，并在交换之后自动扫描修复。
结果与学到：我可以在同一个仓库并行跑多个 Claude Code 会话而不冲突。这是个人仓库里的 23 次提交，不是团队官方工具链。我把自己看作一个 agent 团队的 tech lead，而且仍然拥有每一个 diff。
full_en: Nobody asked for this. Our integration tests run migrations against a shared Snowflake schema, so two engineers, or two AI coding-agent sessions, on different branches collide on DDL. I built a schema pool. Version one cloned from a shared schema whose state depended on who last ran a migration, so version two was a rewrite with three ADRs. In V2 a MAIN schema is synced to whatever commit is actually deployed to production; I query the GitHub Deployments API rather than trust the release tag, because a tag can be cut and never deployed. Each pool slot is a zero-copy clone of MAIN, about two seconds, because a clone copies micro-partition metadata, not data. A session borrows a slot, runs migrations and tests in isolation, and drops it. I also fixed real edge cases: cross-database streams break depending on clone order, so I clone the replication DB before the app DB and auto-detect the pattern after a swap. It's what lets me run several Claude Code sessions in parallel on the same repo. It lives in my own repo, not the team toolchain. I think of it as being the tech lead of a team of agents, and I still own every diff.

hook.zh: 零拷贝克隆，只复制元数据
hook.example: Each pool slot is a zero-copy clone, so it takes about two seconds.
Two agent sessions on different branches collide on DDL in the shared schema.
It's 23 commits in my personal repo, not the team's official toolchain.

starl.zh: 解决自己遇到的小痛点
starl.example: I built the pool to scratch an itch nobody had assigned to me.
V1 taught me that PUBLIC was non-deterministic, so I rewrote it from first principles.

starl.zh: 确定性的，同样输入同样结果
starl.example: Syncing MAIN to the deployed SHA made the slots deterministic.

followups.en: source of truth for what's deployed
followups.zh: “当前部署了什么”的权威来源
followups.example: The Deployments API is the source of truth for what's deployed, not a release tag.
To trust AI code I look at the gates and thresholds, not lines of code.
In money code I read and own every diff.

relp.example: I unblocked myself and the agents by removing the shared-schema bottleneck.

relp.en: tech lead of a team of agents
relp.zh: agent 团队的技术负责人
relp.example: I see myself as the tech lead of a team of agents.
A clone costs metadata rather than storage, so it was a low-cost experiment to run.

full.example: The schema pool was a developer-velocity fix: tests stopped waiting on each other.
The schema pool unblocked parallel work instead of everyone sharing one schema.
Engineers could self-serve an isolated schema in seconds.

senior.q: How would you measure whether the schema pool actually improved developer productivity?
senior.why: 面试官在探：你能否把“感觉更好”变成可度量的结果。
framework: 先选指标：DDL 冲突次数、集成测试排队时间、因共享 schema 重跑的次数
取得基线：用工具之前的几周数据对比
同时看反向指标：同步失败率、槽位泄漏、克隆耗时
说明现状：目前缺少团队级采用数据，我下一步先补埋点
senior.best_practice: 工具价值要用前后对比来证明，只说“好用”不够。我诚实的位置是：它让我能并行跑多个会话，但没有团队级采用数据，所以下一步是先加最小埋点，再谈推广。反向指标同样重要，防止我自己看不见的维护成本。

terms.zh: 基线，改动前的参照数据
terms.example: I need a baseline of DDL collisions per week before claiming an improvement.
I don't have a team-level adoption metric yet, so that's the first thing I'd add.

senior.q: What are the failure modes of a clone-based pool, and how would you keep it reliable as more people use it?
senior.why: 面试官在探：你对共享基础设施的可靠性、泄漏和并发边界是否有思考。
framework: 先列失败模式：槽位泄漏、同步到一半失败、MAIN 与生产漂移、克隆顺序引发的 stream 失效
再说防护：借用设租期、超时自动回收、同步失败有 playbook
监控：槽位使用率、同步新鲜度、克隆耗时
容量：槽位数量与并发会话数的关系，以及耗尽时的退让策略
senior.best_practice: 共享工具的可靠性取决于怎么失败，而不是怎么成功。租期与自动回收防止泄漏，同步新鲜度监控防止测试在过期结构上通过，Sync Failure Playbook 让别人不依赖我也能恢复。这些是个人工具变成团队工具之前必须补的。

terms.example: Isolated clones keep the blast radius of a bad migration to one session.
I'd add a lease and reclaim so abandoned slots free themselves.

senior.q: How do you decide when a personal tool should become the team's official toolchain, and what would you need to change?
senior.why: 面试官在探：你如何把个人创新推向组织采用，并承担责任。
framework: 先看证据：有多少人用、是否解决了真实的高频痛点
再补齐生产化条件：测试、文档、on-call 责任、凭证与权限
与平台或 owner 团队沟通，让他们接手而不是被动接受
给出退出方案：如果不被采用，如何保持个人仓库不影响他人
senior.best_practice: 个人工具缺的通常不是功能，而是责任归属。升级为官方工具链意味着有人长期维护、有 on-call、有权限审计，所以我会先拿采用数据去说服 owner，再决定是否交接。当前它是个人仓库，我会如实这样说，不说成团队标准。

terms.example: Before it becomes official I'd have to productionize it with tests and an owner.
The real question is who takes operational ownership once the team depends on it.

senior.q: You run several AI agents in parallel on one repo. How do you keep quality and safety under control?
senior.why: 面试官在探：你对 AI 辅助开发的工程纪律，而不是只会用工具。
framework: 先说隔离：每个会话独立槽位、独立分支，互不影响
再说流程：和 agent 先做计划，每个阶段先写测试，再实现
质量关卡：CI 与监控的阈值，钱相关代码我逐个读 diff
最后说边界：权限最小化，危险操作需要人确认
senior.best_practice: 并行带来速度，也放大错误，所以隔离和关卡缺一不可。克隆让每个会话互不污染，TDD 和 CI 让错误尽早暴露，对钱相关代码人工读每个 diff，则把最贵的错误挡在人这一层。我看的是关卡和阈值，不是代码行数。

terms.example: Isolation and CI act as guardrails when several agents work in parallel.
For money code I keep a human in the loop and read every diff.
